title: Reflection figures, quarter-wave transformer, lossless line input impedance and guided wavelength

cases.title: VSWR of a 100 ohm load on a 50 ohm line
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: a closed formula on exact inputs, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the terminated lossless line: Gamma = (ZL - Z0)/(ZL + Z0) = 1/3 and SWR = (1 + |Gamma|)/(1 - |Gamma|) = 2

cases.title: Return loss of a 100 ohm load on a 50 ohm line
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the reference is rounded to ten digits
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the terminated lossless line: RL = -20 log10 |Gamma| with |Gamma| = 1/3

cases.title: Mismatch loss of a 100 ohm load on a 50 ohm line
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the reference is rounded to ten digits
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the terminated lossless line: the power delivered to the load is 1 - |Gamma|^2 of the incident power, so the loss is -10 log10 (1 - 1/9)

cases.title: Quarter-wave transformer between 50 and 100 ohm
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: a square root of exact inputs, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the quarter-wave transformer: Z1 = sqrt(Z0 ZL)

cases.title: A quarter-wave line of 50 ohm turns a 100 ohm load into 25 ohm
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the transformation is exact up to the rounding of cos(pi/2)
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the terminated lossless line at l = lambda/4: Zin = Z0^2 / ZL

cases.title: A half-wave line repeats its load
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: exact up to the rounding of sin(pi) and cos(pi)
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the terminated lossless line at l = lambda/2: Zin = ZL

cases.title: Real part of the input impedance of an eighth-wave 50 ohm line closed by 100 ohm
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: with tan(45 deg) = 1 the result is 50 (100 + j50)/(50 + j100) = 40 - j30 exactly
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the terminated lossless line: Zin = Z0 (ZL + j Z0 tan(beta l)) / (Z0 + j ZL tan(beta l))

cases.title: Imaginary part of the same input impedance
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: see the real part; the result is exactly -30 ohm up to rounding
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, the terminated lossless line: Zin = Z0 (ZL + j Z0 tan(beta l)) / (Z0 + j ZL tan(beta l))

cases.title: Wavelength in vacuum at 1 GHz
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: c divided by an exact frequency, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: lambda = c/f with c = 299 792 458 m/s (The International System of Units, the definition of the metre)

cases.title: Guided wavelength at 1 GHz for an effective permittivity of 4
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: c over f over the square root of an exact permittivity, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, TEM lines: lambda = lambda0 / sqrt(er) = c / (f sqrt(er))
